builds.howItPlays: You race to grab battlefields early with cheap units, then start hiding cards face down so your opponent never knows what you're about to spring on them. When the moment is right you flip a hidden card or pull a Teemo unit back to your hand to reset it, ambushing whatever they just committed to the fight.
builds.whyYou: You like being the player your opponent can't read, holding a row of face-down cards that could be anything. You enjoy racing out to an early lead and then switching gears to punish whatever the other player tries next, mixing real threats with bluffs so every one of their decisions feels risky. If you have fun playing mind games as much as playing units, Teemo is your Legend.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 7.5: riftbound.gg says the deck wants to 'grab initiative early on, and score through holding battlefields', and calls the metagame one that rewards 'legends able to go at a hundred miles an hour early on'. stance 6: the same guide describes two phases, aggressive early pressure that later becomes reactive, forcing 'the opponent to take risks, and fall into one of our traps', so it leans proactive on average without being purely so. complexity 7.5: hextechanalytics warns you must 'respect its Hidden capacity and wait until a subsequent turn to play the prepared card' while tracking which facedown slot holds which effect, real bookkeeping. variance 7: hextechanalytics notes 'Strategist's damage varies' and calls the reveal-based damage 'uncertain', a real swing built into the deck's core mechanic. Ability: you may pay 1 Energy to hide a card with Hidden instead of paying its rune cost, and pay 1 Energy plus exhaust Teemo to return a Teemo unit from your Champion Zone or the board to hand. Confidence: medium-high, two independent guides agree closely on the two-phase aggressive-then-disruptive shape of the deck.
